title: Game developers are a dead profession in the next year or two.
author: R_dva
selftext:
We've seen how GPT-Astra creates games. Yes, they lack detail, but it can be added with DLLS 5-6 and GPT will evolve during next years. In this case, game production don’t need a team of 3D artists, and behind them, it don’t need concepters and all other who creates the game content.

  
The gaming market will be flooded with millions of games, and few of them will be profitable. 

  
I am 3d artist, trying understood when this the end comes. What you think?

comments.author: Accomplished-Fan9568
comments.body: Astra made better graphics but is the gameplay actually better?

replies.author: futuneral
replies.body: It made better graphics than Claude, but is it better than what good designers produce?

replies.author: R_dva
replies.body: Who knows, maybe people have already started playing games what made with the GPT-Astra, but they just dont know it

comments.author: CaptainAlexWest
comments.body: Or people make better games then it's like a new banger every couple of weeks. Gta 6 will look like a xbox 360 game in couple of years. Doomers see the end of the world. Ai devs see the golden age of indie games. Social media is rigged and fake. Think for yourself.

replies.author: R_dva
replies.body: I understand that indie development will become easier, but competition would increased hugely with a huge number of indie developers.

replies.author: CaptainAlexWest
replies.body: It been like that for years. Everyone has Google but still people don't build. The question is do you build your skills with it and ride the wave or drown in it. Ai is a tool not a magical game builder. Slop is slop.

comments.author: Jaded_Software_
comments.body:
Same thing will happen that is happening with software engineering. Writing code was just a function of the job, the end result doesn’t change it’s just the deliverables are getting better. You still have to make something people want to use ( or play ) in this case, and that takes more than AI will be able to do anytime in the near future. 

Smaller teams are just going to be able to deliver bigger projects. The demand for software is barely scratching the surface. It’s the same for gaming.

comments.author: KeenAsGreen
comments.body: Designers and writers will still exist. Not much else will though

comments.author: Pristine_Good7326
comments.body: never heard anyone say that painters became a dead profession after the camera was invented, or that novelists became a dead profession after the printer came along.

comments.author: Over-Clerk-5307
comments.body:
I’ve been working with a Claude 20x and Codex Pro 20x every day for about a few months now. I use 100% of my usage every week. 

It seems like the answer is a resounding: no, game dev will not be dead. To me, at least, it seems that it will be the exact opposite; I think we’re entering a renaissance period of good games. 

Go try to make a game with Astra. It’ll give you something, and it will work. But will it be FUN? Astra cannot feel. It cannot experience the joys of solving a puzzle, or the frustration of not knowing what button to click to get to the inventory menu. It doesn’t get terrified during a horror game, and it can’t laugh when your friend does something silly in a friendslop game. 

However, it CAN enable the ability to explore many more creative angles than previously possible. If you have an idea, the friction for exploring and building it is almost 0. But… how many people are willing to sit down for hours and hours and hours to debug their game, or even if functionality is perfect automatically by AI agents, sit down and play something unfun until it’s fun? 

Building a game still requires human intuition and emotional resonance. Astra can certainly achieve games, with minimal human effort (and there will be examples of someone truly one shotting something fun in the near future), but I don’t think that would destroy the industry. If anything, if Joe Shmo can say, “Make fun game now,” and actually get a fun game, then imagine what a game designer of 20 years could do. The amount of unexplored prototypes, expensive ideas, ideas that don’t have the manpower to create — all of those can now be explored. It’s gonna be dope! 

I think AI enables expedited exploration of creativity, if harnessed effectively, and if creativity is held precious as something we’re responsible for. 

And if AI *can* make perfect games and ruin the industry in a single prompt, then man we have much bigger problems societally than games lol

comments.author: meathelix1
comments.body:
I think you have no idea wtf you are on about... There are already millions of games that make zero money.

You are just going to see more now. Its been like this for 10 years, without marketing your game is not going to make any money. And that is part of the problem, if your game is not fun, not different to other games, its going to make no money...

So we will just see more and more bad games and a few that will stand out, like it is already today, just with more slop.
